definition: EU regulation establishing a harmonized framework for AI systems based on risk and obligations.
General Data Protection Regulation governing personal data processing, rights, and enforcement in the EU.
National authority responsible for supervising the application of data protection rules and handling complaints.
The requirement or practice of making the logic, decision factors, and relevant constraints of automated systems understandable to oversight bodies or affected persons.
Policies, controls, and oversight processes used to manage risks across the lifecycle of machine learning or AI models.
A decision taken solely or largely by automated means without meaningful human involvement.
Framework for allocating responsibility when damages or harms arise from AI systems, including fault and risk-based mechanisms.
A large-scale model trained on broad data and adapted for a range of downstream tasks.
The right of individuals to receive meaningful information about the logic involved in automated decisions affecting them.
The obligation of digital platforms to manage risks, disclose information, and remediate harms linked to their services.
